utterance:
Graham, I need to be straight with you, because this is time-critical. Your heart tracing shows you are having a heart attack right now — one of the arteries supplying the bottom of your heart is blocked. That's what the heaviness, the jaw ache and the arm heaviness are; it's not indigestion. The sweating and the sick feeling come from that too.

Here's what I've already done and what happens next:
1. I've called an ambulance (000) to take you straight to hospital. It is on the way. You must not drive yourself, and I'm not letting you walk out of here.
2. I've given you 300 mg of aspirin, chewed and swallowed, to thin the blood and stop the clot growing.
3. Your oxygen level and your chest are fine, so you don't need oxygen.
4. I am deliberately NOT giving you the GTN spray under the tongue. Because you took a Viagra-type tablet last night, that combination can make your blood pressure drop dangerously. No secret between us on this one — I have to tell the paramedics and the hospital doctors you took it, and you must tell them too if they ask. Your privacy is protected, but they need to know to keep you safe.
5. At hospital they'll give you stronger blood thinners and pain relief, repeat blood tests for heart damage — the first one this morning was too early to show anything — and most likely take you straight to the catheter lab to open the blocked artery with a stent. The sooner that's done, the more heart muscle is saved.

Right now: sit back, keep still, and don't eat or drink anything in case you need a procedure. I'll stay with you until the ambulance arrives, and I'll ring your wife so she can come.

You told me you'd been getting tightness climbing ladders this week that eased with rest. That was your heart warning you. Once you're through this, we'll deal with the smoking, your cholesterol and your blood pressure properly — that's how we stop the next one.

If the pain gets worse, you feel faint, or you can't breathe, tell me immediately.
reply: Yeah, I've been sweating like anything. Thought it was just hot. The pain's more heavy than sore, maybe a six. I don't know.

awards.label: Red flag: Sweating or clamminess with the pain

The pain score of six out of ten is from the blocked artery, so the real fix is opening it at hospital; the paramedics will be able to give you strong pain relief with proper monitoring, which is safer than anything I can do here given your slow pulse and your blood pressure.

Three things to remember: don't drive, don't eat or drink, and don't take any more of those erectile tablets — and always tell any doctor or pharmacist you've had one in the last 24 to 48 hours, because combined with the heart spray or patches it can be dangerous.

Once the hospital has treated you, come back and see me within the week. We'll start you on the full set of heart-protective medicines, sort out the cholesterol and blood pressure targets, and get you onto a cardiac rehabilitation program. And the single most powerful thing you can do for your heart from today is to stop smoking — I'll help you with that, and I'll be honest with you: if you keep smoking and keep climbing ladders with that tightness, this will happen again.

You did the right thing coming in today, even if it was your wife who pushed you.
reply: Yeah. I don't know. I just... I don't know.
